review: 1:1 שֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים — John 1:29 (שֵׂה הָאֱלֹהִים); the Arabic حَمَلَ اللهِ is that title, and the Hebrew keeps the Gospel's construct rather than a general 'lamb of God' paraphrase.

3:1 שָׁפֵל בָּאֵבוּס — the Arabic مُتَّضِعًا فِي الْمِذْوَدِ is 'lowly in the manger'; אֵבוּס is the biblical word for the crib (Isa 1:3), and the Hebrew keeps the lowliness as an adjective of the same clause.

2:1–2:2 חֵיק אָבִיךָ … מְעוֹנֶךָ — John 1:18 (בְּחֵיק הָאָב) and 14:2 (מְעוֹנוֹת); the Arabic حِضْنُ أَبِيكَ … سُكْنَاك is that bosom and that dwelling, and the Hebrew keeps the two nouns distinct so the stanza's argument (He was always there) stays visible.
2:3–2:4 the Arabic splits a word across the line break (وَكُنْـ / ـتَ); Hebrew cannot split a word, so the sentence is re-cut whole at the boundary, as in hymn 131.
5:2 עַד־הַדָּם — the Arabic حَتَّى الدَّمِ is 'to the blood'; the Hebrew keeps the preposition of extent (as in Isa 1:18, 'עַד־דָּם'), so the line measures the love rather than naming a quantity.
